## Explanation of the task 2

Task 2 examined whether participants could combine information about estimated voltage
and its uncertainty to locate a relevant spatial region. On each trial, participants saw
one EEG topoplot and were asked to select the scalp region with the highest
signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), defined as the absolute average-referenced voltage divided
by its standard error. They responded using a separate scalp layout divided into 64
selectable regions.

The task included three characteristic ERP patterns: MMN, P3, and N170. Each was shown
using each of the seven visualization types. This produced 21 trials per participant,
each on a separate page. Trial order was randomized separately for every participant.

![Example uncertainty-integration trial. Participants selected one of 64 regions after
identifying the region with the highest SNR.](<../The Art of Uncertain Topoplots/figures/task2_explainer_64_regions.png>){#fig-task2-explainer width=100% fig-alt="An example signal-to-noise-ratio topoplot beside a scalp selection grid divided into 64 regions. A pointer illustrates selecting one region on the grid."}

## Response scoring and trial reconstruction

- For each participan we reconstructed presentation order. Each participant went through 21 randomly shuffled pages.

- For each trial, survey recorded the visualization, ERP stimulus shown
  and one region selected by participant. There were 64 regions on selectable grid.

- The selected region was matched to the corresponding stimulus and its stored region score in `regions.txt`.

- The region score represents |Voltage|/SE at that region. This calcaulation is actually more complicated. 

::: {.callout-note title="How the 0–1 region score was calculated" collapse="true"}

For each stimulus, the scoring pipeline performed the following steps:

1. It loaded one average-referenced ERP case using the task, subject, time point, and
   condition recorded in `task_configs_30_balanced`. The fixed combinations were:

   | ERP pattern | Time point (index) | Condition |
   |:------------|-------------------:|----------:|
   | MMN         |                 96 |         3 |
   | N170        |                105 |         2 |
   | P3          |                129 |         1 |

2. It average-referenced the voltage across the $N$ channels:

   $$
   V_i^{AR} = V_i - \frac{1}{N}\sum_j V_j.
   $$

3. It calculated a polarity-independent, t-like signal-to-noise value at each channel:

   $$
   T_i = \frac{|V_i^{AR}|}{SE_i}.
   $$

4. It interpolated the channel-level $T_i$ values into a continuous topoplot grid. Only
   finite interpolated cells inside the visible head mask were retained.

5. It fitted the saved 64-region polygon template to the topoplot domain. For each
   region $k$, it averaged all retained grid cells that were inside both the polygon and
   the head mask:

   $$
   R_k = \operatorname{mean}\{T(x,y):(x,y)\in\text{region}_k\}.
   $$

6. It min--max normalized the 64 raw region scores separately within each stimulus:

   $$
   S_k = \frac{R_k - \min_j R_j}{\max_j R_j - \min_j R_j}.
   $$

   The weakest region therefore receives 0, the strongest receives 1, and other regions
   are positioned proportionally between them. Scores are rounded to two decimal places.

**Implementation references.** The stimulus-generation source is stored under
`UnfoldMakie/experiments/working/`:

- stimulus selection: `stimuli_data.jl:213`;
- average referencing and channel score: `region_detection/rereferencing.jl:96`;
- topoplot interpolation: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:48`;
- polygon validation and fitting: `get_regions.jl:19`;
- regional averaging: `region_detection/scoring.jl:338`;
- normalization, rounding, and export: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:7`.

The polygon definitions are stored in
`experiments/figures/task2_topo_regions_64_eeg_aligned_pipeline28/regions.jl`.

## Descriptive detection scores

- The analysis contains `r scales::comma(nrow(task2))` responses: `r n_distinct(task2$ID)`
  participants x `r n_distinct(task2$trial)` trials. Each visualization type therefore has
  `r scales::comma(nrow(task2) / n_distinct(task2$vistype))` responses:
  `r n_distinct(task2$ID)` participants x `r n_distinct(task2$pattern)` ERP patterns.

- `r scales::comma(sum(complete.cases(task2)))` of `r scales::comma(nrow(task2))` records
  contain participant, stimulus, visualization type, pattern, position, and score;
  `r sum(!complete.cases(task2))` were excluded for missing model variables.

- Visualization type was treated as a categorical variable, with Basic topoplot as the
  reference condition. ERP pattern and stimulus were retained for the extended model.

- Presentation position was represented by `position_c = position - 11`. Thus,
  `position_c = 0` represents position 11, negative values represent earlier trials, and
  positive values represent later trials.

```{r}
task2_model <- task2 %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    stimulus = factor(stimulus),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    pattern = factor(pattern),
    position_c = as.integer(position) - 11,
    score = as.numeric(score)
  ) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

stimulus_pattern_counts <- task2_model |>
  distinct(stimulus, pattern) |>
  count(stimulus)

stopifnot(
  nrow(task2_model) == nrow(task2),
  all(stimulus_pattern_counts$n == 1)
)
```

```{r task2-score-distribution}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Distribution of the 2,394 trial-level detection scores. Bars show frequencies at
#|   the recorded two-decimal score resolution. A score of 0 indicates selection of the
#|   weakest region for a stimulus, whereas 1 indicates selection of the strongest region.
#|   Intermediate values preserve graded performance.

task2_score_distribution <- task2_model |>
  transmute(score_index = as.integer(round(score * 100))) |>
  count(score_index, name = "responses") |>
  tidyr::complete(
    score_index = 0:100,
    fill = list(responses = 0L)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    score = score_index / 100,
    score_type = if_else(
      score_index %in% c(0L, 100L),
      "Boundary score",
      "Intermediate score"
    ),
    percentage = 100 * responses / sum(responses),
    label_hjust = if_else(score_index == 0L, 0, 1)
  )

stopifnot(
  sum(task2_score_distribution$responses) == nrow(task2_model),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score >= 0),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score <= 1)
)

task2_score_distribution_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_score_distribution,
  aes(x = score, y = responses, fill = score_type)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.009) +
  geom_text(
    data = task2_score_distribution |>
      filter(score_index %in% c(0L, 100L)),
    aes(
      label = sprintf("n = %d (%.1f%%)", responses, percentage),
      hjust = label_hjust
    ),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 5,
    colour = "#111111",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Intermediate score" = "#6BAED6",
      "Boundary score" = "#08519C"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Detection score (0 = weakest region, 1 = strongest region)",
    limits = c(-0.01, 1.01),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Number of responses",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of detection scores") +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20)
  )
```

```{r task2-descriptive-gradient-plot}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Detection scores summarized from participant-level means, with gradient uncertainty.
#|   For each visualization, the black line and number show the mean across participants;
#|   the dark-blue region shows the 95% confidence interval around that mean.

task2_gradient_order <- task2_table |>
  arrange(median) |>
  pull(vistype) |>
  as.character()

task2_gradient_participants <- task2_model |>
  group_by(ID, vistype) |>
  summarise(
    participant_score = mean(score),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task2_gradient_summary <- task2_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_score = mean(participant_score),
    se_score = sd(participant_score) / sqrt(n_participants),
    df = n_participants - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = task2_gradient_order),
    y_position = as.numeric(vistype),
    lower_95 = mean_score - qt(0.975, df) * se_score,
    upper_95 = mean_score + qt(0.975, df) * se_score
  ) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task2_gradient_means <- setNames(
  task2_gradient_summary$mean_score,
  as.character(task2_gradient_summary$vistype)
)
task2_gradient_value <- function(vistype) {
  sprintf("%.2f", task2_gradient_means[[vistype]])
}
task2_gradient_difference <-
  task2_gradient_means[["triple_CI"]] -
  task2_gradient_means[["bivariate_corner"]]

stopifnot(
  all(
    task2_gradient_summary$n_participants ==
      n_distinct(task2_model$ID)
  )
)

task2_gradient_data <- task2_gradient_summary |>
  tidyr::crossing(score = seq(0.5, 0.8, length.out = 241)) |>
  mutate(
    t_distance = abs(score - mean_score) / se_score,
    confidence_level = 2 * pt(t_distance, df) - 1,
    gradient_alpha = if_else(
      confidence_level <= 0.95,
      1,
      pmax(0, (1 - confidence_level) / 0.05)
    )
  )

task2_gradient_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_gradient_data,
  aes(x = score, y = y_position)
) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(alpha = gradient_alpha),
    width = 1 / 800,
    height = 0.62,
    fill = "#6BAED6"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = task2_gradient_summary,
    aes(
      x = mean_score,
      xend = mean_score,
      y = y_position - 0.31,
      yend = y_position + 0.31
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    colour = "#111111"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = task2_gradient_summary,
    aes(

    ),

  ) +

    breaks = seq(0.5, 0.8, 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = task2_gradient_summary$y_position,
    labels = unname(
      vistype_labels[as.character(task2_gradient_summary$vistype)]
    ),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.65))
  ) +
```

## Detection-score analysis

- The primary analysis uses the extended model:

  ```r
  score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)
  ```

- The outcome contains exact 0 and 1 values as well as intermediate scores. An
  ordered-beta model retains this graded information while supporting the complete closed
  interval from 0 to 1. A binary logistic model would instead treat every score below 1
  as equally incorrect.

- Every participant completed 21 trials, so responses from the same participant are
  related. Adding `(1 | ID)` gives each participant their own baseline detection
  performance while estimating common visualization, pattern, and presentation-position
  effects.

- Some stimuli may be intrinsically easier to interpret than others. Adding
  `(1 | stimulus)` gives each stimulus its own baseline score, so visualization
  comparisons are not attributed to stimulus difficulty alone.

- Each stimulus was rendered in all seven visualizations, giving 210 distinct images,
  and each image was seen by about 15 participants. Adding `(1 | stimulus:vistype)`
  gives each image its own deviation from what its stimulus and visualization predict.
  Without it, the responses to one image would count as independent evidence about the
  visualization, although they share whatever made that particular image easy or hard.

- ERP pattern and centered presentation position adjust the visualization comparisons for
  the displayed pattern and for linear change as participants progressed through the task.

- The simpler base model is shown first as a reference. It contains visualization type
  and a participant random intercept but does not adjust for pattern, presentation
  position, or differences among stimuli.

```{r}
model_task2_base <- glmmTMB(
  score ~ vistype + (1 | ID),
  family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_model
)

summary(model_task2_base)$coefficients$cond |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  transmute(
    term = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Basic topoplot (intercept)",
      vistypeadjacent = "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeanimation = "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_range = "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypetriple_CI = "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeuncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot",
      .default = term
    ),
    estimate = Estimate,
    standard_error = .data[["Std. Error"]],
    z_value = .data[["z value"]],
    p_value = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>|z|)"]])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Term",
      "Estimate (logit scale)",
      "Standard error",
      "z value",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Fixed effects for the base sensitivity detection-score model.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Coefficient scale:</strong> Logit scale.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Why correlated participant-specific visualization slopes were not retained" collapse="true"}
We tested whether the effect of visualization type differed between participants by
adding correlated participant-specific visualization effects: `(1 + vistype | ID)`.
The model could not estimate this full structure reliably:

- It ended with convergence code 1, a non-positive-definite Hessian, and singular
  convergence.

- The structure requires seven participant-level random coefficients and 28
  variance--covariance parameters.

- Each participant provided only three detection scores for each visualization type,
  which did not contain enough information to estimate all those parameters reliably.

We also tested simpler participant-specific structures:

- A participant-specific position slope converged, but its estimated standard deviation
  was only 0.006.

- A diagonal visualization structure, `diag(0 + vistype | ID)`, converged with a
  positive-definite Hessian. It estimates separate participant-specific visualization
  variances without estimating their correlations.

We therefore retained participant, stimulus and image random intercepts in the primary model.
This does not show that visualization effects are identical for every participant. It
means that these data cannot reliably estimate the full correlated structure. The
diagonal model remains available as a sensitivity analysis.
:::

```{r}
model_task2_no_vistype <- update(
  model_task2,
  . ~ . - vistype
)

anova(model_task2_no_vistype, model_task2) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model") |>
  mutate(
    model = dplyr::recode(
      model,
      model_task2_no_vistype = "Covariates without visualization type",
      model_task2 = "Covariates with visualization type",
      .default = model
    ),
    `Pr(>Chisq)` = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>Chisq)"]])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Model",
      "Parameters",
      "AIC",
      "BIC",
      "Log likelihood",
      "Deviance",
      "Likelihood-ratio chi-square",
      "df difference",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Likelihood-ratio test of visualization type for detection score.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model family:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed models with a logit ",
    "link.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Full model:</strong> ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + ",
    "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reduced model:</strong> The same model without ",
    "<code>vistype</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Comparison:</strong> The likelihood-ratio test evaluates whether ",
    "adding visualization type improves model fit.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model comparison"
)
```

```{r task2-estimates}
task2_estimates <- emmeans(
  model_task2,
  ~ vistype,
  type = "response"
) |>
  confint() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  transmute(
    vistype,
    predicted_score = response,
    lower_ci = asymp.LCL,
    upper_ci = asymp.UCL
  ) |>
  arrange(predicted_score) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = vistype)
  )

task2_estimates |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    across(
      c(predicted_score, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated detection score",
      "Lower 95% CI",
```

**Figure method.** The points are estimated marginal mean detection scores from
the extended ordered-beta mixed model
`score ~ visualization type + pattern + centered position + (1 | participant) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | image)`,
fitted with a logit link. Estimates are evaluated at the middle presentation
position (`position_c = 0`, corresponding to position 11), averaged equally
over the MMN, N170, and P3 patterns, and calculated with participant, stimulus and
image random intercepts set to zero. They are then back-transformed to the
0–1 detection-score scale. Error bars are asymptotic pointwise 95% confidence
intervals for these model-estimated scores.

### Detection-score differences relative to Basic topoplot

**Figure method.** The contrasts use the same extended model and reference grid
as the estimated-score figure. Estimated marginal means are first
back-transformed to the response scale, and each visualization is then compared
with Basic topoplot. The six confidence intervals use the `emmeans` Dunnett-x
adjustment for multiple comparisons against a common reference. An interval
crossing zero indicates that the corresponding visualization is not clearly
different from Basic at the familywise 95% confidence level.

```{r task2-basic-contrast-figure}
#| cache: false
task2_basic_reference <- which(
```

## Sensitivity analysis: exact-peak responses

- About `r round(100 * mean(task2_model$score == 1))`% of responses have a score of
  exactly 1. Scores are rescaled within each stimulus, so a score of 1 marks the strongest
  region (`r sum(table(region_scores$stimulus[region_scores$score == 1]) > 1)` stimulus
  has two regions tied at 1.00 after rounding to two decimals): these responses are trials
  in which the participant selected the strongest region. The remaining scores describe how
  close a miss was.

- The ordered-beta model handles exact 0 and 1 values, but one linear predictor drives
  both the probability of a 1 and the location of intermediate scores. A visualization
  that helps participants find the exact peak without improving near misses (or the
  reverse) would therefore be averaged into a single effect.

- Two checks address this:
  1. **Posterior predictive check.** Data sets are simulated from the fitted
     ordered-beta model and compared with the observed share of exact-peak responses.
  2. **Two-part model.** A logistic model for finding the exact peak and a beta model for
     the scores of the remaining trials, each with the same predictors and random effects
     as the primary model. Effects in the two parts that differ in direction or strength
     indicate that the single-predictor ordered-beta contrast summarizes two distinct
     effects.

### Posterior predictive check

```{r task2-peak-ppc}
set.seed(20261116)
task2_peak_n_sim <- 1000
task2_peak_sims <- simulate(model_task2, nsim = task2_peak_n_sim)

task2_peak_stats <- function(score, vistype) {
  per_vistype <- tibble::tibble(vistype = vistype, score = score) |>
    group_by(vistype) |>
    summarise(
      share_one = mean(score == 1),
      mean_score = mean(score),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  basic <- per_vistype[per_vistype$vistype == "basic", ]
  per_vistype |>
    mutate(
      share_one_vs_basic = share_one - basic$share_one,
      mean_score_vs_basic = mean_score - basic$mean_score
    )
}

task2_peak_observed <- task2_peak_stats(task2_model$score, task2_model$vistype)

task2_peak_simulated <- purrr::map_dfr(
  task2_peak_sims,
  \(score) task2_peak_stats(score, task2_model$vistype),
  .id = "simulation"
)

task2_peak_ppc <- task2_peak_simulated |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(share_one, share_one_vs_basic, mean_score, mean_score_vs_basic),
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "simulated"
  ) |>
  group_by(vistype, statistic) |>
  summarise(
    lower = quantile(simulated, 0.025),
    median = median(simulated),
    upper = quantile(simulated, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    task2_peak_observed |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-vistype, names_to = "statistic", values_to = "observed"),
    by = c("vistype", "statistic")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    inside = observed >= lower & observed <= upper,
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(task2_model$vistype))
  )

task2_peak_ppc |>
  filter(statistic %in% c("share_one", "share_one_vs_basic")) |>
  filter(!(statistic == "share_one_vs_basic" & vistype == "basic")) |>
  arrange(statistic, vistype) |>
  transmute(
    statistic = if_else(
      statistic == "share_one",
      "Share of exact-peak responses",
      "Difference from Basic topoplot"
    ),
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    observed = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * observed),
    simulated = sprintf(
      "%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
      100 * median, 100 * lower, 100 * upper
    ),
    inside = if_else(
      inside,
      "Yes",
      '<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">No</span>'
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Statistic",
      "Visualization",
      "Observed",
      "Simulated median [95% interval]",
      "Observed inside interval"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Observed versus simulated exact-peak responses (",
      task2_peak_n_sim,
      " data sets simulated from the primary ordered-beta model, ",
      "with new participant and stimulus effects in each simulation)."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

```{r task2-peak-ppc-figure}
  filter(statistic %in% c("share_one", "share_one_vs_basic")) |>
```

### Two-part model

- **Exact peak:** logistic mixed model for `score == 1`.
- **Closeness of misses:** beta mixed model for the trials with `score < 1`. The
  `r sum(task2_model$score == 0)` scores of exactly 0 were moved slightly inward with the
  Smithson–Verkuilen transformation, `(score × (n − 1) + 0.5) / n`.
- Both parts use the primary model's predictors:
  `vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)`.
- The second part is conditional on missing the peak. If a visualization turns near
  misses into exact hits, its remaining misses can look worse even when overall
  performance improves, so the two parts should be read together.

```{r task2-peak-two-part}
task2_peak_hit_model <- glmmTMB(
  peak ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = mutate(task2_model, peak = as.integer(score == 1))
)

task2_peak_miss_data <- task2_model |>
  filter(score < 1) |>
  mutate(score_squeezed = (score * (n() - 1) + 0.5) / n())

task2_peak_miss_model <- glmmTMB(
  score_squeezed ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_peak_miss_data
)

stopifnot(
  task2_peak_hit_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_peak_hit_model$sdr$pdHess),
  task2_peak_miss_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_peak_miss_model$sdr$pdHess)
)

task2_peak_response_estimates <- bind_rows(
  `Probability of exact peak` = emmeans(
    task2_peak_hit_model, ~vistype, type = "response"
  ) |> as.data.frame() |> rename(estimate = prob),
  `Mean score of misses` = emmeans(
    task2_peak_miss_model, ~vistype, type = "response"
  ) |> as.data.frame() |> rename(estimate = response),
  .id = "part"
)

task2_peak_response_estimates |>
  transmute(
    part,
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    value = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", estimate, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization",
      "Probability of exact peak [95% CI]",
      "Mean score of misses [95% CI]"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Model-estimated values from the two-part model, averaged equally over ERP",
      "patterns at the middle presentation position, for a typical participant and",
      "stimulus (random effects at zero)."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

### Visualization effects across models

```{r task2-peak-contrasts}
task2_peak_contrasts <- list(
  `Ordered beta (primary)` = model_task2,
  `Exact peak (logistic)` = task2_peak_hit_model,
  `Misses (beta)` = task2_peak_miss_model
) |>
  purrr::imap_dfr(\(model, name) {
    emmeans(model, ~vistype) |>
      contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "basic", adjust = "none") |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        model = name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        estimate,
        lower = asymp.LCL,
        upper = asymp.UCL
      )
  }) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = unique(model)),
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(task2_model$vistype)),
    excludes_zero = lower > 0 | upper < 0
  )

task2_peak_contrasts |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    model,
    value = if_else(
      excludes_zero,
      sprintf(
        '<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]</span>',
        estimate, lower, upper
      ),
      sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", estimate, lower, upper)
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Visualization vs Basic topoplot", levels(task2_peak_contrasts$model)),
    caption = paste(
      "Differences from Basic topoplot on the logit scale with unadjusted 95%",
      "confidence intervals. Intervals excluding zero are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Scale:</strong> All three columns are on the logit scale: the ",
    "logit of the mean score (ordered beta and misses) or the log-odds of selecting ",
    "the strongest region (exact peak). Directions are comparable; magnitudes are ",
    "not directly comparable across columns.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Multiplicity:</strong> Intervals are not adjusted; this is a ",
    "sensitivity analysis of the primary model's assumption.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Reading the table"
)
```

```{r task2-peak-contrast-figure}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-alt: "Differences from Basic topoplot on the logit scale for the ordered-beta model, the exact-peak logistic model, and the beta model of missed trials, with 95% confidence intervals."
task2_peak_contrasts |>
  mutate(vistype = forcats::fct_rev(vistype)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = vistype)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#377EB8") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.6,
    colour = "#333333"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = excludes_zero), shape = 21, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "white"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) table_vistype(x)) +
  facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Difference from Basic topoplot (logit scale)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Filled red: 95% confidence interval excludes zero (unadjusted)."
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey30")
  )
```

```{r task2-peak-agreement}
task2_peak_agreement <- task2_peak_contrasts |>
  mutate(
    part = case_when(
      model == "Ordered beta (primary)" ~ "primary",
      model == "Exact peak (logistic)" ~ "peak",
      TRUE ~ "miss"
    ),
    direction = case_when(
      !excludes_zero ~ "none",
      estimate > 0 ~ "better",
      TRUE ~ "worse"
    )
  ) |>
  select(vistype, part, direction, estimate) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(direction, estimate)) |>
  rename(primary = direction_primary, peak = direction_peak, miss = direction_miss) |>
  mutate(
    pattern = case_when(
      peak == "none" & miss == "none" ~ "No clear effect in either part",
      peak != "none" & miss != "none" & peak != miss ~
        "Opposite effects on exact peak and misses",
      peak != "none" & miss != "none" ~ "Same effect in both parts",
      peak != "none" ~ paste0(
        "Exact peak only (", if_else(peak == "better", "more", "fewer"), " exact hits)"
      ),
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        "Misses only (", if_else(miss == "better", "closer", "farther"), " misses)"
      )
    ),
    primary_captures = case_when(
      primary == "none" & (peak != "none" | miss != "none") ~
        "No: the ordered-beta contrast shows no clear effect",
      primary != "none" & peak != "none" & peak != primary ~
        "Partly: the exact-peak effect has the opposite direction",
      primary != "none" &
        sign(estimate_peak) != sign(estimate_primary) ~
        "Partly: the exact-peak estimate points the other way (interval includes zero)",
      primary != "none" &
        sign(estimate_miss) != sign(estimate_primary) ~
        "Partly: the miss estimate points the other way (interval includes zero)",
      TRUE ~ "Yes"
    )
  )

task2_peak_agreement |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    pattern,
    primary_captures = if_else(
      primary_captures == "Yes",
      "Yes",
      paste0('<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">', primary_captures, "</span>")
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization vs Basic topoplot",
      "Two-part model",
      "Captured by the primary ordered-beta contrast?"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Agreement between the two-part model and the primary model. An effect counts",
      "when its unadjusted 95% confidence interval excludes zero."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```
